name: AgentDyno-verified trust badge injected into Hugging Face model cards / GGUF repo READMEs
what_it_is: Hugging Face model cards are README.md files with a YAML front-matter metadata block. The metadata natively supports: arbitrary user-defined `tags` (the docs explicitly confirm 'you can add any tag you want', e.g. a `finance` tag); a `base_model` field plus an inferred-or-explicit `base_model_relation` that can be set to `quantized`, `finetune`, `adapter`, or `merge`; and a structured `model-index` eval-results block whose `results[].source` can name and link to an external evaluator (the docs' own example uses `source.name: Open LLM Leaderboard` with a URL), which the Hub parses and renders as a results widget on the model page. Cards also render arbitrary Markdown/HTML, so image 'badges' (shields, ko-fi buttons, GitHub badges) and theme-aware `` logos are routinely embedded. In practice, GGUF quantizers add a semi-standard attribution header: bartowski's cards carry an 'Original model: ', a 'Using llama.cpp release bXXXX for quantization' line, imatrix-dataset credit, a Credits section, and a ko-fi support badge. The nearest existing 'verified for tool-calling' convention is not an on-card badge at all but an external leaderboard: the Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL), which ranks models on executable function/tool-calling and multi-turn agentic tasks, with results centralized at gorilla.cs.berkeley.edu rather than stamped onto model cards.
real_precedent: Hugging Face model-cards documentation (custom tags, base_model_relation: quantized, model-index eval-results with a named/linked `source` such as Open LLM Leaderboard): https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/model-cards . Live GGUF quantizer attribution convention: bartowski/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GGUF card (Original model link, llama.cpp release line, imatrix credit, Credits section, ko-fi badge): https://huggingface.co/bartowski/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GGUF . Existing external tool-calling verification precedent: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (Gorilla): https://github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla/blob/main/berkeley-function-call-leaderboard/README.md
evidence_of_impact: The model-index `source` mechanic is the Hub's officially documented path for an external evaluator (their example is the Open LLM Leaderboard) to have its scores rendered as a card widget and to be filterable/indexable, showing that Hugging Face already sanctions third-party-verification badges on cards: https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/model-cards . For the tool-calling-verification angle, BFCL/Gorilla demonstrates real adoption of a function-calling evaluation authority: its GitHub repo shows 13k stars, 1.4k forks: https://github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla/blob/main/berkeley-function-call-leaderboard/README.md . bartowski's attribution+ko-fi-badge pattern is present across his GGUF cards (verified on the Qwen2.5-7B card), evidencing that community quantizers already voluntarily embed non-official credit/badge blocks that downstream users read: https://huggingface.co/bartowski/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GGUF . [uncertain] Exact download/adoption counts for bartowski repos and whether an AgentDyno badge would actually drive discovery were not independently verified against fetched metrics.
applicability_to_agentdyno: AgentDyno already produces HTML certificates from `dyno` tool-calling verification runs (against Goose/Cline via the local gateway at 127.0.0.1:8403/v1). Add a `dyno publish` / `dyno badge` command that, for a given local GGUF a user pulled (`dyno pull`) and verified (`dyno fit`/`dyno connect`), emits two card artifacts and opens a Hugging Face community PR against the source GGUF repo (or the user's own fork) via `huggingface_hub` create_commit / community-PR API: (1) a Markdown/HTML image badge linking to the hosted certificate, mirroring bartowski's ko-fi-badge pattern; and (2) a `model-index` eval-results block whose `source.name` is 'AgentDyno' with a URL to the reproducible cert, plus a custom `agentdyno-verified` tag and (where the repo is a quant) `base_model_relation: quantized` for discoverability -- reusing the Hub's own Open-LLM-Leaderboard-style `source` mechanic so the result renders as a native card widget rather than a bolt-on. Because the verification specifically measures Goose/Cline tool-calling on the user's actual hardware, the badge asserts something BFCL's server-side leaderboard does not: 'this exact GGUF quant passed agentic tool-calling on local hardware'.
build_effort: small-to-medium. The certificate/HTML generation and the verification data already exist; the new work is (a) templating a YAML `model-index`/tags block + a badge image URL into a README (pure string generation), and (b) wiring `huggingface_hub` auth + create_commit or create_pull_request to inject it into a repo. Hosting the certificate at a stable, fetchable URL (so the badge/source link resolves) is the main new infra dependency. No changes to the scan/fit/serve core are required.
risk_or_caveat: A self-issued badge carries no external trust: unlike Open LLM Leaderboard or BFCL (independent third parties), 'AgentDyno-verified' is the vendor certifying its own users' runs, and image badges are trivially copyable/forgeable, so credibility hinges entirely on the certificate being reproducible and the methodology being public. Opening PRs to inject badges into other maintainers' repos (e.g. bartowski/unsloth) without consent reads as spam and will be rejected or draw backlash; realistically it can only auto-inject into the user's own repos. There is no existing on-card 'agent-ready' tag standard to ride, so an `agentdyno-verified` tag starts with zero recognition and filtering value until a critical mass exists. The mechanic only pays off if AgentDyno's tool-calling verification is itself seen as meaningful.
